title: Cabin Window Frame Surround — Local Strap Repair for Crazing Blend Out

ata.title: Passenger Compartment Windows — Window Frame Structure

abstract: Permanent strap repair for the cabin window frame surround after material has been blended out at a scratch or a corrosion finding, restoring the hoop path around the window cut-out.

sections.purpose: This repair restores the hoop load path around a cabin window cut-out after material has been blended out of the frame surround because of a scratch, a corrosion finding or fastener hole damage at the retainer.
sections.damage_assessment: Measure the residual thickness of the frame surround after blending with the ultrasonic thickness gauge at not less than eight positions around the cut-out. Blending that leaves the thickness inside the allowable limits below needs no repair, only a re-protection. Blending that takes the thickness below the limit, damage that reaches a fastener hole in the retainer land, or damage on a frame that already carries a repair, is repaired by this scheme. A frame with damage at more than two positions around the same cut-out is outside the scope and requires an engineering assessment.
sections.repair_procedure: Remove the window pane assembly and the retainer to the applicable maintenance task, and remove the cabin trim panel to give access to the inner face. Clean the blended area and do a dye penetrant inspection to confirm that no crack remains. Cut the repair strap D5620123830368 to the layout of the repair drawing and offer it to the inner face of the frame surround, following the curvature of the cut-out. Add the gusset D5620126921230 at the lower position where the drawing calls for it, because the lower quadrant carries the higher hoop load. Drill and ream the fastener pattern using the strap as a template, keeping the edge distance on the drawing and staying clear of the retainer land. Deburr and apply the surface protection of the standard practice. Install the strap and the gusset wet with sealant, using screws EN161537K2 at the accessible positions and swaged collars AGS158659-98 where access is single sided. Restore the sealing around the cut-out and refit the retainer, the pane assembly and the trim panel. Do the cabin pressure leak check for the repaired window before the aircraft is returned to service.
sections.inspection_requirements: The repair has no life limit but carries a repeat inspection. Do a detailed visual inspection of the strap perimeter and of the window seal at every heavy check, and an eddy current inspection of the reamed fastener positions every 8 000 flight cycles. A leak at the repaired window, or a new indication at a reamed hole, invalidates the repair. Report the repair to Aeralis with the residual thickness measurements.

type_data.allowable_damage_limits: Blending that leaves at least 85 per cent of the nominal frame surround thickness, at no more than two positions around one cut-out, and no closer than 20 mm to a retainer fastener centre.

repair_drawings.title: Window frame surround strap repair, cabin window cut-out

type_data.fastener_pattern: Single row of 14 screws EN161537K2 each side of the cut-out at 18 mm pitch and 12 mm edge distance, with swaged collars AGS158659-98 at the blind positions
type_data.fatigue_life_note: No life limit. Detailed visual inspection at every heavy check and eddy current inspection of the reamed positions every 8 000 flight cycles.
